links.outcome: Effect of prompt phrasing on guideline alignment and error direction of transfer recommendations
links.effect: Primer 1 and 3 had 77% alignment, primer 2 73% (p=0.24); primer 1 under-referred (93% of misalignments), primers 2 and 3 over-referred (88%, 100%; p<0.001). Burns: primer 1 55% vs 85% (p=0.041).
links.quote: The nature of the errors varied significantly by primer with primer 1 significantly more likely to under-refer (93% of its misalignments), while primers 2 and 3 tended toward over-referral (88% and 100% of misalignments, respectively; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Under-triage and over-triage of interfacility transfer decisions versus guideline gold standard
links.effect: Overall 77% alignment (23% misalignment); primer 1 mostly under-referred, primers 2 and 3 mostly over-referred.
links.quote: This finding is clinically meaningful, as under-triage in emergent settings could delay care, whereas over-triage may unnecessarily burden specialist services.
